spans.s:
वैशद्य (द्यं) 1.
n. Whiteness, purity.

वैशम्पायन (नः) 1.
m. A sage, teacher
of the
Yajur Veda.

वैशस (सं) 1.
n. Hindrance; slaugh-
ter; distress, cruelty.

वैशस्त्र (स्त्रं) 1.
n. Government, rule;
state of being defenceless.
a.
Miserable.

वैशाख (खः)
m. Name of a month
(April-May); a churning stick.
n. Attitude in shooting.
f. (खी).
Day of the full moon in the a-
bove month.

वैशारद (दः-दा-दं)
a. Wise.

वैशिक (कं) 1.
n. Harlotry.

वैशेषिक (कः) 1.
m. A follower of the
[]
Vaisheshika doctrine.
a. That
doctrine, or branch of the
Nyāya
school.

वैशिष्ठ्य (ष्ठ्यं) 1.
n. Being possessed
of; distinction.

वैश्य (श्यः)
m. Man of the 3d class.

वैश्य-वृत्ति (त्तिः) 2.
f. Idem.

वैश्रम्भक (कं) 1.
n. A particular para-
dise or celestial grove.
a. Con-
fiding in.

वैश्रवण (णः) 1.
m. Kuvera, god of
wealth.

वैश्रवणा_लय (यः) 1.
m. The Indian fig tree.

वैश्रवणा_वास (सः) 1.
m. Idem.

वैश्रवणो_दय (यः) 1.
m. Idem.

वैश्व-देव (वः-वी-वं)
a. Of all divi-
nities, or of the
Vishwadevas. n.
An offering to them.
f. Name
of a metre.

वैश्वदेव-कर्म्मन् (र्म्मा) 5.
n. Offering to
all divinities.

वैश्वदेव-होम (मं) 1.
n. Offering to the
Vishwadevas.

वैश्वानर (रः-री-रं) 1.
m. Agni or fire.
f. A sacrifice at the beginning
of the year.
a. Intended for all
the world.

वैश्वी (श्वी) 3.
f. 21st constellation.

वैषम्य (म्यं) 1.
m. Inequality, solitari-
ness; difficulty; injustice.

वैषयिक (कः) 1.
m. A sensualist.

वैष्टुत (तं) 1.
n. The ashes of a burnt-
offering.

वैष्ट्र (ष्ट्रं) 1.
n. A world.

वैष्णव (वः-वी-वं)
a. Relating or
belonging to
Viṣṇu. m. A fol-
lower of him.
f. (वी) A divine
energy,
Durgā; sacred basil.

वैसारिन (नः) 1.
m. A fish.

वैसादृश्य (श्यं) 1.
n. Variety.

वैसूचन (नं) 1.
n. A man's assum-
ing female attire in the drama.
